purpose: Challenge whether full self-closure, start self-closure, end self-closure and ordinary linkage are four structural states of pole distinction/resolution without redefining the ostensive signs as functions or opcodes.

researchReading.fullyOpen: no external pole distinguished in this resolution act; root meaning remains semantically primary
researchReading.startOpen: end e distinguished while start remains self-closed/open
researchReading.endOpen: start b distinguished while end remains self-closed/open

resolutionCandidate.readKnownComplete: known X=(b,e) resolves b and e directly from the same relation
resolutionCandidate.readStartOpen: known S=(S,e) resolves the already distinguished e
resolutionCandidate.readEndOpen: known E=(b,E) resolves the already distinguished b

rootBoundary.reason: this challenge tests compatibility of that interpretation but does not reduce root semantics to interpreter state

requiredAssertions: start-open and end-open forms are finite cyclic binary links
both partial branches resolve to one exact complete pair for the same b/e bindings
resolution does not mutate either partial relation
form inversion maps start-open(e) to an end-open form over e and vice versa
known complete relation exposes its two poles without redefining self-closure glyphs as projections
known start-open exposes its distinguished end and known end-open exposes its distinguished start
multiple start-open refs may satisfy the same known end shape
multiple end-open refs may satisfy the same known start shape
partial-form multiplicity does not violate exact-pair uniqueness
a legitimate self-closed relation is not globally marked incomplete
no semantic stage tag, Meaning node, or host Optional/Pair ontology is embedded in Link
notDecided: whether the four forms are accepted universal interpretation semantics
whether R is the canonical fully-open state for every interpretation act
whether root abits are instances of these forms or serialization meanings derived from them
general associative-memory query language for partial forms
formal notation syntax for relation solving
